messages:
michael: heads up, model-serving in eu-edge is misrouting requests after the egress gateway rotate, looks like headless svc traffic keeps going to a dead pod IP 
anya: ugh, saw that earlier. are you seeing 503s or just timeouts?
michael: timeouts + occasional 502 from envoy. kubectl logs show connections to 10.244.12.43 which was terminated last night
michael: ran `kubectl get endpointslices -n model-serving --selector=app=model -o wide` and still shows the old ip in one slice
anya: hmm, could be kube-proxy cache / iptables rules not cleaned up after the NAT translation changed
raj: devops-bot just alerted about a rolling restart of the egress gateway at 02:03 UTC, conntrack entries might have sticky SNATs
leah: can you paste iptables-save or `iptables -t nat -L -n --line-numbers` from a node?
michael: here's a snippet from node-edge-7: ```
Chain KUBE-SERVICES (2 references)
num  target     prot opt source               destination
1    DNAT       tcp  --  0.0.0.0/0            10.96.100.5:80 to:10.244.12.43:8080
```
michael: and `kubectl describe pod model-a-5` shows it was evicted at 01:45 and recreated at 02:10 with new ip 10.244.55.9
anya: so iptables DNAT is still pointing at the old pod IP -> kube-proxy didn't update rules for that node
raj: which kube-proxy mode are we running on the edge clusters? ipvs or iptables?
leah: edge clusters are mostly iptables mode, and we recently switched endpointSlice feature gate on. could be a watch glitch where endpointSlice controller updated slice but kube-proxy missed the event
sre-oncall: automated fix: try `kubectl rollout restart daemonset/kube-proxy -n kube-system` on the affected nodes, that forces rule reconciliation. doing a full rolling DS restart is low-risk for these nodes
michael: tried restarting kube-proxy on node-edge-7, rules updated and traffic restored :) but this will be noisy if we do it coast-to-coast
anya: we should root cause: if egress gateway rotation leaves old SNATs, conntrack may keep NAT mapping and kube-proxy may not garbage-collect when endpoint changed. we saw similar flakiness in canary last month
raj: logging for endpointSlice watch lag? we can enable `--v=4` on kube-proxy for a short window and check for dropped watch events
leah: also consider switching kube-proxy to ipvs on edge clusters — ipvs heals faster for frequent endpoint churn, but requires kernel modules and grooming
sre-oncall: short term runbook: 1) drain node if it's misbehaving; 2) restart kube-proxy DS on node; 3) clear conntrack entries for the old pod IP `sudo conntrack -D -s 10.244.12.43` if you need immediate recovery; 4) open an incident if it repeats >3x in 24h
michael: adding that to the incident notes. one more data point: `tcpdump -i eth0 host 10.244.12.43` showed SYNs still hitting that IP even after pod gone, so conntrack definitely sticky
anya: followup action: add a short probe to check for endpoint->iptables/route divergence in the console dashboards and alert if mismatch >30s
leah: i'll file a ticket to evaluate ipvs migration for eu-edge and add a kube-proxy health check for endpointSlice watch latency
raj: i'll also add a pre-rotation hook for egress gateway that sweeps conntrack on affected nodes to avoid SNAT stickiness
sre-oncall: noted. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
